conceptZh: 圓滾滾的扭蛋小怪獸追著從畫面邊緣探頭的「爸」字，大怪獸爸爸和小怪獸爸爸輪流躲貓貓，最後上面的「父」和下面的「巴」安靜坐好。
object: a round fuzzy pocket creature bursting from a gachapon capsule, and a much bigger fuzzy creature parent peeking in from the edges
morph: the upper part 父 and lower part 巴 of 爸 keep sneaking in from the edges and dodging, then settle stacked in place
creativeAngle: 躲貓貓：字的上半「父」和下半「巴」輪流從畫面邊緣探頭、閃開，小怪獸追不到，最後大怪獸現身，兩半一起落位。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and warm, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-mint backdrop with a soft cream floor. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated tomato-red Traditional Chinese glyph 爸, the 父 component stacked on top of the 巴 component, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins. The lead is an original round fuzzy orange pocket creature with big eyes and stubby feet that pops out of a split gachapon capsule and bounces off everything; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the capsule cracks open at center and the little creature boings out, bouncing off the floor and the left wall; the first spoken 爸 lands as the red 父 shape pokes in from the top edge, waves its strokes like a hello, and zips back out of sight. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): the creature spins around, confused, and chases it; the red 巴 slides up from the bottom edge, pokes its hook out, then ducks behind the capsule shell; the creature lifts the shell and finds nothing, eyes crossed, and the second spoken 爸 lands as both halves leap out from opposite edges and dodge him once more. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): the creature stamps his foot, puffs up round as a ball, and a second, much bigger fuzzy creature with a gentle smile lifts him up in one soft paw; the two halves rush in and click together into 爸 as the word 爸爸 is spoken, the little creature clapping its paws. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 爸 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in red; the big creature sets the little one on its shoulder, and the little one waves both arms and wobbles with joy, far from the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「爸、爸、爸爸」, read as ㄅㄚˋ、ㄅㄚˋ、ㄅㄚˋ ㄅㄚ˙, first utterance at about 0.6s, second at about 2.8s, the word at about 4.4s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only soft boings and a gentle chime under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠想推倒一排立著的紅色骨牌，先戳不動、再助跑摔個狗吃屎，鼻子一碰骨牌就連環倒下，倒平的骨牌一塊接一塊排成上面的「父」和下面的「巴」，最後一塊翹翹板把小老鼠彈上天，落在「巴」的勾尾上比了個傻傻的讚；念「爸爸」時，鬍子老鼠爸爸從旁邊探進來把他扛上肩膀。
object: a domino run of tall standing tomato-red tiles laid out along the stroke paths of 爸, with the very last tile a long seesaw plank, plus a tiny cheeky grey mouse and a big mustached papa mouse who appears only for the word
morph: the standing tiles topple one after another; each lands flat and butts against the next so the fallen tiles form the solid red strokes, 父 on top first, then faster around the box of 巴, and the final seesaw plank slams down as the hook stroke while catapulting the mouse up to land on its tip
creativeAngle: 與前一版「躲貓貓拼字」完全不同：這次是「骨牌連鎖」實體笑料，小老鼠先想推、再助跑摔倒、鼻子一碰引爆連環倒下，倒下的骨牌本身就是筆畫，從慢到快、最後翹翹板把他彈飛落在勾尾上，因果一眼看懂。第二角色沒有用拉布拉多警長，因為「爸爸」這個詞需要畫面上真的出現一位爸爸，所以改用一隻大鬍子老鼠爸爸只在念詞時探頭把他扛上肩，單一配角、不加人群。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip with a locked frontal camera, bright warm lighting, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale butter-yellow backdrop with a soft cream floor and nothing else behind. The only on-screen text is one correctly formed, bold, saturated tomato-red Traditional Chinese glyph 爸 (the 父 component stacked on top of the 巴 component, standard stroke shapes), centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with generous margins when finished. Cast: the lead is an original tiny cheeky cartoon grey mouse with huge round pink ears, a long whippy tail and a permanent grin, lightning fast and proud of it; later ONE supporting character, a big round original papa mouse with a bushy mustache and a cozy knitted cardigan. No real people, no branded characters, no presenter.

Moment one, want it (0.0-1.5s): center stage already holds a neat domino run of tall red standing tiles, arranged along the stroke paths of 爸, the top rows tracing 父 and the lower rows tracing 巴, with the very last tile at the bottom right a long red seesaw plank balanced on a little block. The little mouse zips in from the left, skids to a stop, stares up at the first tile at the top-left, rubs its paws together and pokes it with one finger. The tile wobbles and stays up. The first spoken 爸 lands here at about 0.7s as the finger poke happens.

Moment two, try and miss (1.5-3.0s): the mouse backs way up to the left edge, winds up with a huge cartoon arm-spin, sprints at the tile, trips over its own tail and face-plants into a long belly-slide, stopping with just its nose tapping the first tile. The tile tips. Click-clack, the top tiles fall one after another, each landing flat and butting against the next so the fallen tiles line up into the solid red strokes of 父, dot, dot, then the crossing strokes. The second spoken 爸 lands at about 2.6s exactly as the last tile of 父 slaps down and 父 snaps complete.

Moment three, the big crash (3.0-5.0s): the chain races downward and speeds up, tiles clattering faster and faster around the box shape of 巴, the mouse scrambling alongside trying to outrun them and bumping its bottom on a falling tile so it lands dazed on the raised end of the seesaw plank. Frozen half-beat of anticipation. The second-to-last tile slams the other end of the plank: the plank drops flat as the final hook stroke of 巴 while the mouse is catapulted high into the air, spinning twice with squash-and-stretch, and plops down right on the tip of the hook as the glyph 爸 completes with a soft bonk. It wobbles, goes cross-eyed, then gives a surprised thumbs-up and hops off to the right side of the frame.

Moment four, the payoff (5.0-8.0s): the finished glyph 爸 stays perfectly still, crisp and unobstructed for the full final 3 seconds. At about 5.3s the word 爸爸 is spoken exactly as the big mustached papa mouse pops in from the right edge, scoops the dizzy little mouse up and sets it on his shoulders; the two sway and wave, well away from the strokes, the little mouse patting papa's head, until the end at 8.0s.

Narration (off-screen only, warm friendly Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, Taiwan standard reading, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「爸、爸、爸爸」, read as ㄅㄚˋ、ㄅㄚˋ、ㄅㄚˋ ˙ㄅㄚ, first utterance at about 0.7s, second at about 2.6s, the word at about 5.3s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only soft click-clack domino sounds, a gentle boing and a tiny bonk under the voice, quieter than the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter, no flashing effects.
